open_points.subject: MigrationClosure identity across restored store histories
open_points.text: “it is a fact about the store's history”; “that history then holds its own closure”; but M10 remains a `value`, and “two records of ‘the migration succeeded at instant T’ would mean the same thing”
open_points.question: When a backup containing a MigrationClosure is restored and thereby starts a new store history, is the restored closure the same value copied from the former history, or a distinct history-scoped closure—and, if distinct, what makes the store history part of its identity?
options: The closure is a content value copied unchanged into the new history and is the same value across histories.
Each store history owns a distinct singleton closure, with history scope participating in identity even if no history identifier is stored.
Restoration creates a new closure derived from the backed-up closure, with facts identifying that derivation.
open_points.default_guess: Treat MigrationClosure as a history-scoped singleton: restoration carries its recorded facts forward, but the closure occurrence belongs to the new store history and is not newly minted by an import.
